candidate.title: TruSeq Small RNA
candidate.scope: The single unbranched Illumina TruSeq Small RNA schematic, from a small RNA fragment through adaptor ligation, primer addition, reverse transcription, and denaturation/amplification to an indexed P5/P7-flanked library ready for cluster generation. No alternative workflow or kit revision is identified. Cluster generation and sequencing are downstream interfaces, not depicted operations.

states.label: Small RNA fragment
features: Single purple strand; 5′ end at left and 3′ end at right.
No specific terminal phosphate, hydroxyl or other modification is indicated.

evidence.locator: Top material: purple single strand labeled 5′ at left and 3′ at right; Small RNA fragment

states.label: 5′ and 3′ adaptors
features: Magenta 5′ adaptor and green 3′ adaptor, identified by labels in the ligation product.

evidence.rationale: The Ligate adaptors caption and the two newly attached labeled segments establish adaptor addition; the unligated adaptors are not drawn separately.

evidence.locator: First downward arrow and Ligate adaptors caption; product with 5′ Adaptor (magenta) and 3′ Adaptor (green) flanking the purple insert

evidence.locator: Second downward arrow and Add primer caption; short lower green strand paired with the right-hand green adaptor

states.label: Reverse-transcription product: RNA with complementary DNA

evidence.rationale: The named reverse-transcription step and added strand identify the lower strand as cDNA copied from the adaptor-ligated RNA.

features: Primer extensions depicted as orange P5 at left and Index 1/P7 at right.
Their annealed arrangement is an internal intermediate of Denature and amplify, not a claim that the primers are already bound before that combined operation.

evidence.locator: Denature and amplify region: downward arrows, separated strands, P5 and Index 1/P7 primer extensions, and final double-stranded product
evidence.rationale: The Denature and amplify region shows short annealed segments with outward P5 and Index 1/P7 tails; these are interpreted as the amplification-primer inputs whose extensions appear in the final product, not as a separate workflow branch.

states.label: Indexed DNA library ready for cluster generation
features: Double-stranded product with blue insert corresponding to the reverse-transcribed small RNA.
Left orange P5 region, adaptor-derived magenta and green regions, and right-hand Index and P7 regions.
The index is a separate flanking segment, not the biological small-RNA insert.

evidence.locator: Bottom: paired strands with left P5, central blue insert, right Index and P7; Product ready for cluster generation
Reverse transcription through final product
evidence.rationale: The continuous arrows carry the copied small-RNA insert through amplification into the final paired-strand product; this is the DNA library carrier of the original RNA sequence information.

operations.label: Ligate adaptors
operations.description: Attach the depicted 5′ and 3′ adaptors to opposite ends of the small RNA, producing one adaptor-flanked RNA strand. The combined caption does not resolve the order of the two ligations.
operations.mechanism: Ligation, as labeled; no particular enzyme or terminal chemistry is specified.
operations.information_effect: The purple small-RNA insert remains between distinct terminal adaptor regions.

evidence.locator: First downward arrow and Ligate adaptors caption; product with 5′ Adaptor (magenta) and 3′ Adaptor (green) flanking the purple insert

operations.label: Add primer
operations.description: Add a primer that is shown bound to the 3′-adaptor region of the adaptor-ligated RNA, creating the substrate for reverse transcription.
operations.mechanism: Primer binding is represented by the short paired segment at the right-hand adaptor.
operations.information_effect: Positions the primer at an adaptor-defined site adjacent to the RNA insert.

evidence.locator: Second downward arrow and Add primer caption; short lower green strand paired with the right-hand green adaptor

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Extend from the bound primer to make a complementary DNA strand across the adaptor-ligated RNA; the output drawing retains the upper RNA with the new lower strand.
operations.mechanism: Primer-directed reverse transcription, identified by the caption and the new complementary strand.
operations.information_effect: Transfers small-RNA sequence information into a complementary DNA carrier.

evidence.locator: Third downward arrow and Reverse transcription caption; long lower blue strand beneath the purple RNA
Reverse transcription caption and newly extended lower strand
evidence.rationale: Reverse transcription names the RNA-to-DNA copying transformation; the new strand drawn along the RNA indicates the copied sequence association.

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: Process the reverse-transcription product through the depicted separated-strand and tailed-primer intermediate, then amplification to the final paired-strand library. P5 and index/P7 extensions in this region become the flanking segments of the final product. Denaturation and amplification remain one local operation under the shared caption.
operations.mechanism: Strand separation and primer-mediated amplification as depicted; cycle conditions and handling of the RNA strand are not specified.
operations.information_effect: Retains the small-RNA-derived insert in an amplified DNA library and adds the depicted index and P5/P7 interface. Subsequent insert sequencing could identify represented small-RNA sequences; sequencing itself is outside the drawing, which establishes neither complete RNA capture nor absolute molecule abundance.
